claim: Four age-stratified cross-sectional surveys of approximately 2000 participants per survey were conducted in Bongo District, Ghana, in October 2012, October 2014, October 2015, and October 2017.
source: Four age-stratified cross-sectional surveys of ~2000 participants per survey were conducted in Bongo, Ghana, at the end of the wet seasons in October 2012 (Survey 1, baseline pre-IRS, red), October 2014 (Survey 2, during IRS, orange), October 2015 (Survey 3, post-IRS, green), and October 2017 (Survey 4, SMC, purple)
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states the survey design and timing, and Figure 1A provides visual representation of the study timeline.

claim: Three rounds of IRS with non-pyrethroid insecticides were implemented in Bongo District between 2013 and 2015.
source: Between 2013 and 2015, three rounds of IRS with non-pyrethroid insecticides were implemented across all of Bongo District (Figure 1A).
evidence: The manuscript directly states the intervention details with reference to Figure 1A.

claim: IRS reduced transmission intensity by more than 90% as measured by the entomological inoculation rate (EIR).
source: We document P. falciparum prevalence, as well as var diversity and population structure from baseline in 2012 through a major perturbation by a short-term indoor residual spraying (IRS) campaign managed under operational conditions, which reduced transmission intensity by >90% as measured by the entomological inoculation rate (EIR)
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states the reduction in transmission intensity measured by EIR.

claim: IRS decreased parasite prevalence by approximately 40-50%.
source: which reduced transmission intensity by >90% as measured by the entomological inoculation rate (EIR) and decreased parasite prevalence by ~40–50% (Tiedje et al., 2022)
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states the reduction in parasite prevalence with citation to supporting work.

claim: The prevalence of microscopic P. falciparum infections declined by 45.2% following the second round of IRS (2012-2014).
source: Coincident with the >90% decrease in transmission following IRS (Tiedje et al., 2022), the prevalence of microscopic P. falciparum infections compared to the 2012 baseline survey (pre-IRS) declined by 45.2% and 35.7% following the second (2012–2014) and the third (2012–2015) round of IRS, respectively (Figure 1B, Appendix 1—table 1).
evidence: The manuscript provides specific percentage decline with reference to data tables and figures.

claim: The prevalence of microscopic P. falciparum infections declined by 35.7% following the third round of IRS (2012-2015).
source: Coincident with the >90% decrease in transmission following IRS (Tiedje et al., 2022), the prevalence of microscopic P. falciparum infections compared to the 2012 baseline survey (pre-IRS) declined by 45.2% and 35.7% following the second (2012–2014) and the third (2012–2015) round of IRS, respectively (Figure 1B, Appendix 1—table 1).
evidence: The manuscript provides specific percentage decline with reference to data tables and figures.

claim: Younger children (1-5 years) were approximately 3 times less likely to have an infection in 2015 (post-IRS) compared to 2012 (pre-IRS).
source: These declines in parasite prevalence were observed across all ages, with the greatest impacts being observed on the younger children (1–5 years) who were ~3 times less likely to have an infection in 2015 (post-IRS) compared to 2012 (pre-IRS) (Figure 1C, Appendix 1—table 1).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states the relative risk reduction for younger children with reference to data.

claim: In 2017, 32 months after the discontinuation of IRS, overall P. falciparum prevalence rebounded to 41.2%, near pre-IRS levels.
source: These reductions were, however, short-lived and in 2017, 32 months after the discontinuation of IRS, but during SMC, overall P. falciparum prevalence rebounded to 41.2%, or near pre-IRS levels (Figure 1B, Appendix 1—table 1).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states the rebound in prevalence with specific percentage and timing.

claim: The increase in prevalence of infection in 2017 was only observed among older age groups (≥6 years).
source: Importantly, this increase in the prevalence of infection in 2017 was only observed among the older age groups (i.e. ≥6 years) (Figure 1C, Appendix 1—table 1).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states the age-specific pattern of prevalence rebound.

claim: The difference in prevalence by age group in 2017 can be attributed to SMC, which only targets children between 3 and 59 months.
source: This difference by age group in 2017 can be attributed to SMC, which only targets children between 3 and 59 months (i.e. <5 years).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly attributes the age-specific difference to SMC targeting.

claim: A notable increase in parasite prevalence for adolescents (11-20 years) and adults (>20 years) was found in 2017 relative to 2012 (pre-IRS).
source: A notable increase in parasite prevalence for adolescents (11–20 years) and adults (>20 years) was found in 2017 relative to 2012 (pre-IRS) (Figure 1C, Appendix 1—table 1).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states the increase in prevalence for specific age groups.

claim: Median PTS values for both upsA and non-upsA DBLα types remained low in all surveys.
source: Figure 2 shows that median PTS values for both upsA and non-upsA DBLα types remained low in all surveys
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this finding with reference to Figure 2.

claim: The PTS distributions for both upsA and non-upsA DBLα types changed significantly at each study time point relative to the 2012 baseline survey (p-values<0.001, Kruskal-Wallis test).
source: although the PTS distributions for both groups changed significantly at each of the study time points relative to the 2012 baseline survey (pre-IRS) (p-values<0.001, Kruskal-Wallis test) (Figure 2).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states the statistical significance of changes in PTS distributions.

claim: The change in PTS was in the direction of reduced similarity (less overlap) with lower median PTS scores and a larger number of isolates sharing no DBLα types in 2014, 2015, and 2017 compared to 2012.
source: Somewhat unexpectedly, the change was in the direction of reduced similarity (i.e. less overlap) with lower median PTS scores and a larger number of isolates sharing no DBLα types (i.e. PTS = 0) in 2014, 2015, and 2017 compared to 2012.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly describes the direction and nature of the change in PTS.

claim: The median PTS scores for non-upsA DBLα types were lower following the IRS intervention (PTSnon-upsA: 2014=0.013 and 2015=0.013 vs. PTSnon-upsA: 2012=0.020).
source: Relevant to the measurement of MOIvar, the median PTS scores for non-upsA DBLα types were lower following the IRS intervention (PTSnon-upsA: 2014=0.013 and 2015=0.013 vs. PTSnon-upsA: 2012=0.020).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly provides specific median PTS values for comparison.

claim: In 2017, the non-upsA PTS distributions shifted back toward higher median PTS scores (PTSnon-upsA=0.016) and fewer isolates shared no DBLα types relative to 2014 and 2015.
source: In 2017, the non-upsA PTS distributions shifted back toward higher median PTS scores (PTSnon-upsA=0.016) and fewer isolates shared no DBLα types relative to 2014 and 2015 (Figure 2).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly describes the shift in PTS distributions in 2017.

claim: 99.9% of the isolate comparisons in all surveys had PTSnon-upsA scores ≤0.1 (shared ≤10% of their non-upsA DBLα types).
source: These PTS data make clear that we were dealing with a large, highly diverse parasite population where 99.9% of the isolate comparisons in all surveys had PTSnon-upsA scores ≤0.1 (i.e. shared ≤10% of their non-upsA DBLα types), indicating that DBLα isolate repertoires were highly unrelated (Figure 2).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly provides the percentage of isolate comparisons with low PTS scores.

claim: Less than 0.003% isolate comparisons in each survey had a PTSnon-upsA≥0.5 (siblings or recent recombinants).
source: In fact, throughout the IRS, SMC, and subsequent rebound, very few DBLα isolate repertoires were observed to be related, with <0.003% isolate comparisons in each survey having a PTSnon-upsA≥0.5 (i.e. siblings or recent recombinants) (Figure 2).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly provides the percentage of related isolate comparisons.

claim: At baseline in 2012, the majority (89.2%) of the population across all ages carried multiclonal infections with a median MOIvar=4 [IQR: 2-6].
source: We observed that at baseline in 2012, the majority (89.2%) of the population across all ages carried multiclonal infections (median MOIvar=4 [interquartile range (IQR): 2–6]) (Figure 3A).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states the proportion and median MOIvar at baseline.

claim: Following the IRS intervention, the estimated MOIvar distributions became more positively skewed, indicating that a lower proportion of participants harboured multiclonal infections with a lower median MOIvar in 2014 (64.5%; median MOIvar=2 [IQR: 1-3]) and 2015 (71.4%; median MOIvar=2 [IQR: 1-3]) compared to 2012.
source: Following the IRS intervention, the estimated MOIvar distributions became more positively skewed, indicating that a lower proportion of participants harboured multiclonal infections with a lower median MOIvar in 2014 (64.5%; median MOIvar=2 [IQR: 1–3]) and 2015 (71.4%; median MOIvar=2 [IQR: 1–3]) compared to 2012 (Figure 3A).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly describes the changes in MOIvar distributions following IRS.

claim: Reductions in median MOIvar and the proportion of multiclonal infections were observed across all age groups following IRS.
source: These reductions in median MOIvar and the proportion of multiclonal infections, which were observed across all age groups (Figure 3B), are consistent with the >90% decrease in transmission intensity following the IRS in turn reducing exposure to new parasite genomes.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states the age-specific reductions in MOIvar.

claim: In 2017, both the median MOIvar (3 [IQR: 2-4]) and the proportion of multiclonal infections (78.9%) rebounded in all age groups.
source: However, in 2017, both the median MOIvar (3 [IQR: 2–4]) and the proportion of multiclonal infections (78.9%) rebounded in all age groups, even among the younger children (1–5 years) predominantly targeted by SMC (Figure 3).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states the rebound in MOIvar and multiclonal infections in 2017.

claim: While the prevalence of infection in 2017 remained low for younger children (1-5 years), those infected still carried multiclonal infections (84.1% of those infected).
source: While the prevalence of infection in 2017 remained low for the younger children (1–5 years), those infected still carried multiclonal infections (84.1% of those infected) (Figure 3B).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states the proportion of multiclonal infections among infected younger children in 2017.

claim: In 2014 during IRS, census population size decreased by 71.4% relative to the 2012 baseline survey (pre-IRS).
source: In 2014 during IRS, this number decreased by 71.4% relative to the 2012 baseline survey (pre-IRS) (Figure 4C and E), whereas prevalence decreased by 54.5% (Figure 4C and E).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states the percentage decrease in census population size.

claim: In 2015, there were 64.4% fewer var repertoires in the population compared to 2012.
source: Although census population size increased slightly in 2015 relative to 2014 (Figure 4A), there were still 64.4% fewer var repertoires in the population compared to 2012 (Figure 4C and E) in comparison to a 42.6% decrease in prevalence (Figure 4C and E).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states the percentage decrease in var repertoires.

claim: The loss of var repertoires in 2014 and 2015 following the IRS intervention was seen for all age groups, with the greatest overall reductions (≥83.8%) being observed for the younger children (1-5 years).
source: Importantly, this loss of var repertoires in 2014 and 2015 following the IRS intervention was seen for all age groups (Figure 4B), with the greatest overall reductions (≥83.8%) being observed for the younger children (1–5 years) (Figure 4D and F).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states the age-specific reductions in var repertoires.

claim: In 2017, the number of diverse var repertoires in the population rebounded, more than doubling between 2015 and 2017.
source: However, in 2017, the number of diverse var repertoires in the population rebounded, more than doubling between 2015 and 2017 (Figure 4C and E).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states the rebound in var repertoires.

claim: The increase in the number of var repertoires in 2017 was seen for all age groups except for the younger children (1-5 years) where those up to 59 months were targeted by SMC.
source: This increase in the number of var repertoires was seen for all age groups in 2017, except for the younger children (1–5 years) where those up to 59 months were targeted by SMC (Figure 4B and D).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states the age-specific pattern of var repertoire rebound.

claim: The greatest overall increase in var repertoires was observed for the adolescents (11-20 years) and adults (>20 years), where the number of var repertoires in 2017 was approximately 1.2 times higher compared to 2012.
source: In fact, the greatest overall increase was observed for the adolescents (11–20 years) and adults (>20 years), where the number of var repertoires in 2017 was ~1.2 times higher compared to 2012 (Figure 4F).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states the magnitude of increase for specific age groups.

claim: Richness at baseline in 2012 (pre-IRS) was high with a large number of unique DBLα types (upsA = 2218; non-upsA=33,159).
source: Richness at baseline in 2012 (pre-IRS) was high with a large number of unique DBLα types (upsA = 2218; non-upsA=33,159) (Figure 5, Appendix 1—table 3)
evidence: The manuscript explicitly provides the number of unique DBLα types at baseline.

claim: In 2014, there was a 32.2% and 55.3% reduction in richness for the upsA and non-upsA DBLα types, respectively, compared to 2012.
source: In 2014, as P. falciparum prevalence and census population size declined (Figure 4), so too did the number of DBLα types, resulting in a 32.2% and 55.3% reduction in richness for the upsA and non-upsA DBLα types, respectively, compared to 2012 (Figure 5, Appendix 1—table 3).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states the percentage reduction in richness.

claim: In 2015, DBLα type richness was still less than that observed in 2012 (24.6% and 46.0% reduction for upsA and non-upsA DBLα types, respectively).
source: Again in 2015, as P. falciparum prevalence and population size remained low (Figure 4), DBLα type richness was still less than that observed in 2012 (24.6% and 46.0% reduction for upsA and non-upsA DBLα types, respectively) (Figure 5, Appendix 1—table 3).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states the percentage reduction in richness for 2015.

claim: In 2017, upsA and non-upsA DBLα type richness rebounded relative to 2014 and 2015, coincident with the increase in P. falciparum prevalence and census population size.
source: Finally, in 2017, we found that upsA and non-upsA DBLα type richness rebounded relative to 2014 and 2015, coincident with the increase in P. falciparum prevalence and census population size (Figures 4 and 5).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states the rebound in richness in 2017.

claim: Individual upsA and non-upsA DBLα types were not all at equal frequencies within a survey and among surveys.
source: We discovered that individual upsA and non-upsA DBLα types were not all at equal frequencies within a survey and among surveys.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states the variation in DBLα type frequencies.

claim: DBLα types could be classified as frequent (observed in 11-20 or >20 isolates), less frequent (observed in 2-10 isolates), or only seen once, at baseline in 2012.
source: They could be classified as frequent (i.e. observed in 11–20 or >20 isolates), less frequent (i.e. observed in 2–10 isolates), or only seen once, at baseline in 2012 (Figure 6AB).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly defines the frequency categories for DBLα types.

claim: In 2014 and 2015, following IRS, there was a significant increase in the proportion of upsA and non-upsA DBLα types in the lower frequency categories (p-value<0.001, Mann-Whitney U test), with all DBLα types becoming rarer in the population.
source: In 2014 and 2015, following IRS, there was a significant increase in the proportion of upsA and non-upsA DBLα types in the lower frequency categories (p-value<0.001, Mann-Whitney U test), with all DBLα types becoming rarer in the population (Figure 6CD).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states the statistical significance of changes in DBLα type frequency distributions.

claim: The shift to all DBLα types becoming rarer following IRS changed in 2017, where the proportion of DBLα types in the more frequent categories significantly increased while the proportion seen once decreased (p-values<0.001, Mann-Whitney U tests).
source: This shift to all DBLα types becoming rarer following IRS changed in 2017, where the proportion of DBLα types in the more frequent categories (i.e. 2–10, 11–20, or >20 isolates) significantly increased while the proportion seen once decreased (p-values<0.001, Mann-Whitney U tests) (Figure 6C and D).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states the statistical significance of changes in DBLα type frequencies in 2017.

claim: The upsA DBLα types persisted significantly longer in the population relative to the non-upsA DBLα types (p<0.001, log-rank test), despite the IRS intervention.
source: To explore this observation further, we restricted the longitudinal analysis to those DBLα types from the baseline survey in 2012 (pre-IRS). We compared the probability of survival for the DBLα types identified at baseline in 2012 and found that the upsA DBLα types persisted significantly longer in the population relative to the non-upsA DBLα types (p<0.001, log-rank test), despite the IRS intervention.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states the statistical significance of differential persistence between upsA and non-upsA types.

claim: The upsA and non-upsA DBLα types that were observed at multiple study time points were those that were most frequent (observed in 11-20 and >20 isolates) in the population at baseline in 2012.
source: Furthermore, when we examined survival using the frequency categories, the upsA and non-upsA DBLα types that were observed at multiple study time points (i.e. 2012, 2014, 2015, and 2017), albeit in different isolate repertoires, were those that were most frequent (i.e. observed in 11–20 and >20 isolates) in the population at baseline in 2012 (Figure 6E and F).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states the relationship between baseline frequency and longitudinal persistence.

claim: The DBLα types that were only observed once in 2012 were significantly less likely to be seen longitudinally (p-value<0.001, log-rank test).
source: As expected, the DBLα types that were only observed once in 2012 were significantly less likely to be seen longitudinally (p-value<0.001, log-rank test) (Figure 6E and F).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states the statistical significance of reduced persistence for rare types.

claim: Census population size is distinct from effective population size (Ne) as measured by neutral variation.
source: The sum of these antigenically distinct infections over all sampled hosts provides us with a census of the parasite count of relevance to monitoring and evaluating malaria interventions. We refer to this census population size hereafter simply as population size but make clear that this measure is distinct from effective population size (Ne) as measured by neutral variation.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly distinguishes census population size from effective population size.

claim: Varcoding employs an approximately 450 bp region of a var gene, known as a DBLα tag encoding the immunogenic Duffy-binding-like alpha (DBLα) domain of P. falciparum erythrocyte membrane protein 1 (PfEMP1).
source: This method employs an ~450 bp region of a var gene, known as a DBLα tag encoding the immunogenic Duffy-binding-like alpha (DBLα) domain of P. falciparum erythrocyte membrane protein 1 (PfEMP1), the major surface antigen of the blood stages (Zhang and Deitsch, 2022).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly describes the molecular basis of varcoding with citation.

claim: Bioinformatic analyses of a large database of exon 1 sequences of var genes showed a predominantly 1-to-1 DBLα-var relationship, such that each DBLα tag typically represents a unique var gene, especially in high transmission.
source: Bioinformatic analyses of a large database of exon 1 sequences of var genes showed a predominantly 1-to-1 DBLα-var relationship, such that each DBLα tag typically represents a unique var gene, especially in high transmission (Tan et al., 2023).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states the relationship between DBLα tags and var genes with citation.

claim: The extensive diversity of DBLα tags, together with the very low percentage of var genes shared between parasites, facilitates measuring MOI by amplifying, pooling, sequencing, and counting the number of unique DBLα tags (or DBLα types) in a host.
source: The extensive diversity of DBLα tags, together with the very low percentage of var genes shared between parasites (Chen et al., 2011; Day et al., 2017; Ruybal-Pesántez et al., 2022; Ruybal-Pesántez et al., 2017), facilitates measuring MOI by amplifying, pooling, sequencing, and counting the number of unique DBLα tags (or DBLα types) in a host (Ruybal-Pesántez et al., 2022; Tiedje et al., 2022).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly describes how DBLα diversity enables MOI measurement with citations.

claim: Bongo District is located in the Upper East Region of northern Ghana, one of the 12 highest burden countries in Africa.
source: Here, we report an investigation of changes in parasite census population size and structure through two sequential malaria control interventions between 2012 and 2017 in Bongo District located in the Upper East Region of northern Ghana, one of the 12 highest burden countries in Africa (World Health Organization, 2022).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states the location and burden status with citation.

claim: Malaria in high-transmission endemic areas of sub-Saharan Africa is characterised by vast diversity of the Plasmodium falciparum parasites from the perspective of antigenic variation.
source: Malaria in high-transmission endemic areas of sub-Saharan Africa (SSA) is characterised by vast diversity of the Plasmodium falciparum parasites from the perspective of antigenic variation (Chen et al., 2011; Day et al., 2017; Otto et al., 2019; Ruybal-Pesántez et al., 2022; Ruybal-Pesántez et al., 2017).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this characteristic with multiple citations.

claim: Children experiencing clinical episodes of malaria eventually become immune to disease but not to infection.
source: As with other hosts of hyper-variable pathogens (Futse et al., 2008), children experiencing clinical episodes of malaria eventually become immune to disease but not to infection.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this immunological pattern with citation.

claim: There is a large reservoir of chronic asymptomatic infections, in hosts of all ages, sustaining transmission to mosquitos.
source: This results in a large reservoir of chronic asymptomatic infections, in hosts of all ages, sustaining transmission to mosquitos.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states the existence and role of the asymptomatic reservoir.

claim: The majority of people in high-transmission endemic areas harbour diverse multiclonal infections measured as the complexity or multiplicity of infection (MOI).
source: Studies of P. falciparum genetic diversity have shown that the majority of people in high-transmission endemic areas harbour diverse multiclonal infections measured as the complexity or multiplicity of infection (MOI) (e.g. Anderson et al., 2000; Paul et al., 1995; Smith et al., 1999; Sumner et al., 2021) with complex population dynamics (Bruce et al., 2000; Farnert et al., 1997).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this characteristic of high-transmission areas with citations.

claim: Varcoding is more sensitive to measure MOI in high transmission where there is an extremely high prevalence of multiclonal infections that cannot be accurately phased with either biallelic SNP panels or combinations of single copy antigen genes.
source: Prior work has shown that varcoding is more sensitive to measure MOI in high transmission where there is an extremely high prevalence of multiclonal infections that cannot be accurately phased with either biallelic SNP panels (Ghansah et al., 2023; Labbé et al., 2023; Tessema et al., 2022; Watson et al., 2021) or combinations of single copy antigen genes (Sumner et al., 2021).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states the superior sensitivity of varcoding with citations.

claim: The parasite population remained very large and retained the var population genetic characteristics of a high-transmission system (high var diversity; low var repertoire similarity), demonstrating the resilience of P. falciparum to short-term interventions in high-burden countries of sub-Saharan Africa.
source: Despite major perturbations from IRS and SMC interventions, the parasite population remained very large and retained the var population genetic characteristics of a high-transmission system (high var diversity; low var repertoire similarity), demonstrating the resilience of P. falciparum to short-term interventions in high-burden countries of sub-Saharan Africa.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this conclusion about parasite resilience.

claim: DBLα sequencing data was obtained from 2397 P. falciparum isolates (93.2%).
source: DBLα sequencing data was obtained from 2397 P. falciparum isolates (93.2%) (Appendix 1—table 3).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states the sequencing success rate.

claim: Using a cut-off of ≥20 DBLα types to ensure robust downstream analyses, DBLα sequencing data was obtained from 2099 P. falciparum isolates (81.6%) with a total of 289,049 DBLα sequences and 53,238 unique DBLα types being identified in the study population.
source: Using a cut-off of ≥20 DBLα types to ensure robust downstream analyses, DBLα sequencing data was obtained from 2099 P. falciparum isolates (81.6%) with a total of 289,049 DBLα sequences and 53,238 unique DBLα types being identified in the study population (Appendix 1—table 3).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly provides the sequencing data summary with quality threshold.

claim: The median P. falciparum density was approximately 4 times higher for isolates with ≥20 DBLα types compared to those that gave no or <20 DBLα types (520 [IQR: 200-1880] parasites/μL vs. 120 [IQR: 40-200] parasites/μL, respectively).
source: The median P. falciparum density was ~4 times higher for isolates with ≥20 DBLα types compared to those that gave no or <20 DBLα types (520 [IQR: 200–1880] parasites/μL vs. 120 [IQR: 40–200] parasites/μL, respectively).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly compares parasite densities between sequencing success groups.

claim: The proportions of upsA and non-upsA var genes in a repertoire or single genome have been defined as approximately 15-20% and approximately 80-85%, respectively, based on whole-genome sequencing.
source: The proportions of upsA and non-upsA var genes in a repertoire or single genome have been defined as ~15–20% and ~80–85%, respectively, based on whole-genome sequencing (Rask et al., 2010).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states the expected proportions with citation.

claim: The median proportions of upsA and non-upsA DBLα types at the repertoire level were comparable in 2012 (19% upsA and 81% non-upsA), 2014 (22% upsA and 78% non-upsA), 2015 (21% upsA and 79% non-upsA), and 2017 (20% upsA and 80% non-upsA).
source: The upsA and non-upsA DBLα type proportions were partitioned as expected in our analyses, with the median proportions at the repertoire level being comparable in 2012 (19% upsA and 81% non-upsA), 2014 (22% upsA and 78% non-upsA), 2015 (21% upsA and 79% non-upsA), and 2017 (20% upsA and 80% non-upsA).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly provides the observed proportions across all surveys.

claim: PTS is a similarity statistic to evaluate the proportion of DBLα types shared between two isolate repertoires (DBLα repertoire overlap) and ranges from 0 (no DBLα repertoire overlap) to 1 (identical DBLα isolate repertoires).
source: PTS, analogous to the Sørensen index, is a similarity statistic to evaluate the proportion of DBLα types shared between two isolate repertoires (i.e. DBLα repertoire overlap) and ranges from 0 (i.e. no DBLα repertoire overlap) to 1 (i.e. identical DBLα isolate repertoires), where <0.50 = unrelated, 0.5=recent recombinants/siblings, >0.5 = related, and 1=clones.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly defines PTS and its interpretation.

claim: PTS is a measure of identity-by-state used to assess repertoire similarity between isolates and is not used to infer inheritance from a recent common ancestor (IBD).
source: PTS is a measure of identity-by-state used to assess repertoire similarity between isolates and is not used to infer inheritance from a recent common ancestor (i.e. IBD) (Speed and Balding, 2015).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly distinguishes PTS from IBD with citation.

claim: The non-upsA DBLα types were chosen to calculate MOIvar since they are more diverse and less conserved between isolate repertoires compared to the upsA DBLα types.
source: To calculate MOIvar, the non-upsA DBLα types were chosen since not only are they more diverse and less conserved between isolate repertoires (i.e. low median PTSnon-upsA ≤0.020) compared to the upsA DBLα types, but they have also been shown to have a more specific 1-to-1 relationship with a single var gene than upsA (Tan et al., 2023).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly justifies the choice of non-upsA types for MOIvar calculation.

claim: Self-reported LLIN usage from the previous night remained high across all age groups: from 89.1% in 2012 (pre-IRS), 83.5% in 2014 (during IRS), 90.6% in 2015 (post-IRS), to 96.8% in 2017 (SMC).
source: Over the course of this study, self-reported LLIN usage from the previous night remained high across all age groups: from 89.1% in 2012 (pre-IRS), 83.5% in 2014 (during IRS), 90.6% in 2015 (post-IRS), to 96.8% in 2017 (SMC).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly provides LLIN usage data across all surveys.

claim: IRS coverage in Bongo District was 91.8% in Round 1, 95.6% in Round 2, and 96.6% in Round 3.
source: Based on AGAMal's operational reports, IRS coverage in Bongo District was 91.8% in Round 1, 95.6% in Round 2, and finally 96.6% in Round 3 (AGAMal, personal communication).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly provides IRS coverage data.

claim: The monthly EIR declined by more than 90% at the peak of the wet season between August 2013 (pre-IRS) (EIR = 5.3 ib/p/m) and August 2015 (post-IRS) (EIR = 0.4 ib/p/m).
source: Using these surveys, we observed that the monthly EIR (infective bites/person/month [ib/p/m]), a measure of local transmission intensity, declined by >90% at the peak of the wet season between August 2013 (pre-IRS) (EIR = 5.3 ib/p/m) and August 2015 (post-IRS) (EIR = 0.4 ib/p/m) (Tiedje et al., 2022).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly provides EIR data showing transmission reduction.

claim: SMC is the intermittent administration of a curative dose of an antimalarial to children between the ages of 3-59 months.
source: SMC is the intermittent administration of a curative dose of an antimalarial to children between the ages of 3–59 months (i.e. <5 years) (WHO, 2012).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly defines SMC with citation.

claim: The SMC drug combination of choice in Ghana is sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine plus amodiaquine, which is administered at monthly intervals during the high-transmission season.
source: Like other countries, the SMC drug combination of choice in Ghana is sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine plus amodiaquine, which is administered at monthly intervals (i.e. ~28–30 days apart) during the high-transmission season (i.e. wet season) (WHO, 2012).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly describes the SMC regimen with citation.

claim: Reported SMC coverage in Bongo District was 92.6% in 2016 (two cycles between August and September 2016) and 94.6% in 2017 (four cycles between July and October 2017).
source: Reported SMC coverage in Bongo District was 92.6% in 2016 (two cycles between August and September 2016) and 94.6% in 2017 (four cycles between July and October 2017) (Gogue et al., 2020; NMEP/GHS, personal communication).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly provides SMC coverage data.

claim: Census population size proved more informative than parasite prevalence alone because it captures 'within' host parasite population size as MOI, rather than using the infected host per se as a unit of population size.
source: Census population size proved more informative than parasite prevalence alone because it captures 'within' host parasite population size as MOI, rather than using the infected host per se as a unit of population size.
